- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to over-forecast, especially after sharp spikes — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If model shows strong upward momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive rising forecasts) with negative sentiment, it often overshoots — cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high or adjust downward by 2–5%.
- When sentiment is positive (e.g., > 0.3) and model is rising, check for mean reversion — if price has been rising >10% over 5 days, reduce forecast slope by 10–20%.
- If model forecast is consistently higher than true outcome by >3% over 3–5 days, apply downward bias correction — subtract 1–3% from next 3–5 forecast points.
- If sentiment is volatile or mixed (±0.2–0.3), model often overfits short-term noise — use 3-day moving average of true values as baseline for correction.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows early sharp decline (e.g., first 3 days drop >2%), model often fails to adjust — reduce forecast by 2–5% for first 3 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.3 → -0.3 → +0.3), model tends to lag — add 1–2% lag correction to forecast for next 3–5 days.
